description: Read-only cross-site slow-path guidance. Strategies never change permissions, contracts, validators, budgets, route state, or terminal decisions.

applies_when: A page exposes repeated items such as a list, table, grid, or card collection.
Target fields are visible text or attributes within each repeated item.
The collection can be explored through semantic perception and ordinary scrolling.
procedure: Confirm page state, then use DOM.getAXTree to identify item boundaries, labels, controls, and stable anchors.
Scroll only when more items must be materialized; refresh DOM.getAXTree after scrolls.

Enumerate stable canonical ids from the current AXTree, then use one native targets batch for related DOM.getText or DOM.getAttribute reads; inspect each response.data.items entry independently and preserve target order when rebuilding rows.
Persist rows with record_extraction using exact expected_artifact field names.
success_criteria: required row count is satisfied
row keys match expected_artifact
critical fields have page evidence
duplicates or empty critical fields are handled by validators
failure_signatures: items are not materialized after scroll
rows lack stable text or attributes
critical fields are derived only from loop index or visual position
record_extraction field names do not match expected_artifact

applies_when: The target output is mainly non-text attributes such as href, src, id, aria-*, data-*, or value.
The visible label and attribute source should be tied back to the same semantic item or control.
procedure: Use DOM.getAXTree to locate the item/control/anchor associated with each attribute.
Use DOM.getAttribute for the target attribute value.
Use DOM.getText only to bind visible labels to the extracted attributes.
Avoid building URLs or attributes from string guesses when DOM.getAttribute can read them.
Persist rows with sourceSelectorOrAxId and pageUrl when attributes are critical.
success_criteria: attributes are non-empty when required
URLs or ids satisfy validators
visible labels are bound to the same source element or item
row keys match expected_artifact
failure_signatures: attribute value is guessed from visible text
label and attribute come from unrelated nodes
relative/absolute URL handling is undocumented
selector is too fuzzy to identify one source element

applies_when: A page contains named sections or detail regions whose bodies may need reveal actions.
Reveal mechanisms may include tabs, accordions, show-more buttons, anchor links, or scroll-triggered lazy loading.
The target output is section text, section structure, or section availability.
procedure: Use DOM.getAXTree to locate headings, controls, tab labels, accordion buttons, show-more controls, anchor links, and section bodies.
Reveal hidden or lazy content through Input.click or Input.scroll only when the AXTree shows an appropriate control or target.
Refresh DOM.getAXTree after each reveal action and verify the intended state or subtree changed.

Use DOM.getSemanticTree when required section text is absent from AXTree but present in the semantic DOM; use DOM.getText for focused final text and DOM.getAttribute for ids, real hrefs, or state attributes.
If the page shell exists but multiple expected sections remain missing, treat content completeness as unresolved rather than recording empty values or target_absent.

When a search/listing source exists, save sourcePageId/sourceUrl and stable item identity, take a Page.list inventory snapshot, then click one freshly rebound real anchor and inspect Page.list plus Page.getState before the next action; classify NEW_TAB, SAME_TAB, IN_PAGE, or NO_EFFECT from returned page and DOM feedback.

When a tool result includes routeRecovery, follow its structured return method and requiredActions. Honor routePreference only inside its task-local source-template/cohort scope and discard it after challenge/auth change, selector drift, NO_EFFECT, or missing required-region markers.

For a new-tab detail, return with Page.switchTo(sourcePageId); for a same-tab detail, return with Page.go back one history entry and then refresh Page.getState plus DOM.getAXTree. Use Page.navigate(sourceUrl) only as fallback.
If listing-link recovery remains available, report route_sensitive_content_suppression; after its bounded attempts are exhausted, report blocked_content_suppression instead of target_absent.

For a uniform repeated collection, enumerate item/field canonical ids and batch DOM.getText/DOM.getAttribute. If records require scrolling or load-more materialization, repeat the same native AXTree + batch-read cycle after one bounded materialization action and deduplicate locally; do not use page JavaScript or local_fs as live state.
success_criteria: section presence or absence is explicit
final text or records come from the selected structured DOM tool with cited page evidence
reveal actions are verified before extraction
navigation-click outcomes are classified from Page/DOM feedback
listing state is restored with switchTo or history back before the next item
explicit repeated-record targets meet their requested count inside the target subtree
row keys match expected_artifact
failure_signatures: text is only a form prompt or placeholder
click did not change target state or subtree
visible selector points to a container unrelated to the target section
section body was summarized without DOM text evidence
page shell success was mistaken for content completeness
a drawer shell or loading skeleton was mistaken for materialized records
a same-tab detail returned by direct navigation instead of history without a recorded fallback reason

applies_when: Native DOM.getAXTree, DOM.getText, and DOM.getAttribute cannot express a required computed relationship.
The required relation involves geometry, cross-node aggregation, shadow DOM, cross-frame content, or non-DOM browser state.
A native DOM cross-check can still validate at least one target field.
procedure: Call browser_call(method=Runtime.evaluate) only with runtime_policy containing intent, effect, a valid reason_kind, why_structured_tools_insufficient, cross_check_plan, and result_mode, and set params.world=isolated. Never request auto or main directly.
Keep JavaScript scoped to the computed relationship; do not use it for text or attributes native DOM tools can read.

For result_mode=json, pass a JSON-serializable value expression or invoked IIFE, never a function body with top-level return or an uninvoked function. For non_dom_state only, throw ReferenceError('ABCP_MAIN_WORLD_REQUIRED:<global>') when the required page global is absent in isolated world; the harness may then run one explicit strict main retry and records both attempts. Ordinary errors, timeouts, and empty values never authorize main.
Cross-check target fields with DOM.getText or DOM.getAttribute before record_extraction.
If cross-check is impossible, finalize with an explicit blocker rather than handing off unverified target data.
success_criteria: reason_kind is valid
computed value is JSON-serializable
critical fields have native DOM cross-check evidence
record_extraction documents source and cross-check
failure_signatures: reason is generic or circular
JavaScript returns non-serializable objects
target fields have no DOM cross-check
Runtime.evaluate is used for ordinary text/attribute extraction

applies_when: The task requires interacting with controls, entering values, submitting a form, or verifying an action result.
Controls can be found through labels, roles, names, or accessible state.
procedure: Locate controls and labels with DOM.getAXTree.
Fill values with Input.type/Input.press and toggle/select with Input.click using AXTree ids or stable selectors.
Verify entered values with DOM.getAttribute(value) or refreshed AXTree state.
Before submit/save, call Page.getState to catch unexpected dialogs or navigation state.
After submit/save, verify the result with Page.getState, DOM.getAXTree, DOM.getText, or visual_verify only when DOM evidence is insufficient.
success_criteria: target controls receive intended values
submit/save result is verified
blocking dialogs/overlays are handled or reported
final state evidence is persisted when required
failure_signatures: control label cannot be tied to input
entered value is not reflected in DOM state
submission outcome is assumed without verification
CAPTCHA/login/payment/permission wall blocks completion

applies_when: Input.click reports that the target element is occluded or mouse action is blocked.
DOM.getText or DOM.getAttribute returns a visibility, viewport, or occlusion warning.
DOM.getAXTree shows a dialog, alertdialog, login prompt, banner, or overlay covering target content.
procedure: Call dismiss_overlay once with the blocked target id/selector and original method; the composite owns close-control and Escape through native actions, plus AXTree disappearance checks. Coordinate backdrop/VL clicks are unavailable without an independent native point hit-test.
Treat auth/login and paywall blocked results as terminal for automatic dismissal; do not click provider, payment, consent-submit, or login controls.
Retry the original action at most once and only when dismiss_overlay reports that retry is safe; otherwise follow its structured blocker/next-step result.
If the overlay persists after the bounded composite, report the blocker instead of hand-running or repeating the dismissal ladder.
success_criteria: overlay disappearance is verified
the original action is retried at most once after dismissal
sensitive login/payment/provider buttons are not clicked automatically
failure_signatures: overlay persists after Escape/backdrop/close attempts
dismiss action caused navigation or clicked a sensitive submit control
the same occluded click is repeated without refreshing DOM.getAXTree

applies_when: A login or account prompt blocks the task and the dismiss ladder cannot clear it.
The user may have an existing authenticated fleet/session for the same origin.
The task should avoid repeated manual login across workers.
procedure: Treat auth memory as an index only: use Memory scope auth_fleet_sessions_v1 with kind auth_fleet_session_index for origin/account label to fleetId and verification timestamps, never as a credential store.
Before using a remembered fleetId, verify Fleet.status or Page.create can revive it, then open the origin and confirm the login prompt is gone.
If the remembered session is stale, mark it stale in Memory and continue with the normal blocker flow.
If no reusable session exists, call Hitl.requestPause with a purpose that asks the user to complete login and keep the tab/fleet open.
After HITL login resumes, verify the page is usable and save a refreshed auth-session memory entry for future workers.
success_criteria: a reused fleet is verified before task continuation
expired sessions are marked stale instead of reused blindly
no plaintext credentials or private tokens are stored in Memory
failure_signatures: remembered fleet is archived, missing, or still shows the auth prompt
Memory contains credentials instead of session metadata
worker repeatedly asks for login without checking auth memory

applies_when: A page may require human login, CAPTCHA, approval, payment confirmation, or manual review.
The worker is considering Hitl.requestPause or has just resumed from HITL.
discouraged_tools: calling Hitl.resolvePause from the worker after requestPause
procedure: Before requesting HITL for ordinary overlays, first verify page state and run the overlay dismiss ladder when it is safe.
Use Hitl.requestPause only for CAPTCHA, hard auth walls, sensitive approval, manual review, or overlays that cannot be safely dismissed.
Treat an unpredicted login, QR/SMS/2FA prompt, CAPTCHA, or human-verification gate as a runtime interrupt of the current worker; do not finalize solely to hand it to a new auth or HITL worker.

A generic sign-in header alone is insufficient. Once Page.getState plus DOM.getAXTree show an authentication or verification surface, concrete auth controls or methods, and protected content that is blocked or inaccessible, call Hitl.requestPause immediately.

Inspect every depth-zero rootwebarea in DOM.getAXTree, including embedded frames. A challenge-labelled frame with a slider, checkbox, or verification button is decisive structural evidence even when the main page looks normal; let the harness enter HITL without requiring whole-page VL confirmation.

After decisive DOM evidence, do not reread the same offloaded AXTree, record a gate-only artifact, take screenshots, or call visual_verify unless the evidence is ambiguous, contradictory, or primarily graphical.
After Hitl.requestPause succeeds, the harness owns wait, resolve, and confirmation; do not call Hitl.resolvePause yourself.

Continue the original worker contract only when hitl_wait.status is resumed, after Page.getState and a fresh DOM.getAXTree verify that the challenge frame is gone; then retry the interrupted reveal/materialization checkpoint and verify the requested target record count. Otherwise finalize with a blocker.
success_criteria: HITL is reserved for genuine user action requirements
the worker does not self-resolve its own pause
post-HITL page state is re-synchronized before DOM/Input actions
post-HITL business content is revalidated instead of accepting the page shell
failure_signatures: Hitl.requestPause is used for a dismissible overlay before trying safe dismissal
Hitl.resolvePause is called by the worker after requestPause
worker continues DOM/Input calls while the page is paused
whole-page VL normal_loading overrides a challenge iframe with an actionable verification control
worker resumes after HITL but accepts a skeleton or drawer shell without revalidating target records
